verdict.rationale: kitty ships its own documented remote-control CLI for controlling the terminal from scripts or the shell. A hands-on runtime probe confirmed `kitten @ ls` returns window, tab and layout state as JSON, and that `send-text`, `get-text` and `close-window` complete an external agent-control loop. Missing for 10: an in-depth first-party CLI command reference (flags, output formats) in the pack, and independent community corroboration of CLI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: kitty can be controlled from scripts or the shell prompt. You can open new windows, send arbitrary text input to any window, change the title of windows and tabs, etc.

`kitten @ ls` returned full window/tab/layout state as JSON, `kitten @ send-text "echo PA_PROBE_OK"` executed in the live window, `kitten @ get-text` read the output back, `kitten @ close-window` tore it down — complete external agent-control loop verified hands-on.
